handbook.title: Deposit handbook
handbook.subtitle: The most valuable thing we give you — knowing the law keeps your money.
handbook.disclaimer: This is general information, not legal advice. For personal help: Shelter 0808 800 4444 (free) or gov.uk.

s1.title: Before you pay
s1.intro: Don't lose money before you even have keys.
items: Never hand over cash without a receipt — a bank transfer with a clear reference is best.
The legal maximum deposit = 5 weeks' rent (for rent under £50,000/year). £520/month rent → £600 max deposit.
Check you're paying the right person: the landlord's name on the contract must match their verified RentAPlace profile.
Only pay after you've seen the room (in person, or on a live video call from inside the room).

s2.title: After you pay — the 30-day rule
s2.intro: Within 30 days of you paying, the landlord must protect the deposit in a government scheme and send you the paperwork. Demand all of it:
items: ① A receipt confirming the deposit amount.
② The protection certificate, naming the scheme: DPS, mydeposits or TDS.
③ The 'prescribed information' — a required info pack (address, amount, how you get the deposit back).
④ Check it yourself, free, on the scheme's website — you just need the deposit ID, or your surname + postcode + tenancy start date.
s2.checkerLinks: Check your deposit: DPS · mydeposits · TDS — free, takes a minute.

s3.title: Your leverage
s3.intro: If 30 days pass and the deposit isn't protected, or you haven't received the paperwork:
items: Step 1 — Send a demand letter (we have templates in Vietnamese + English). Most landlords comply the moment they see you know the law.
Step 2 — If they still don't: you can claim in the county court for 1 to 3× the deposit (the court decides the multiple). A £600 deposit → a possible £600–£1,800 award, plus the deposit itself.
A landlord with an unprotected deposit also can't use the standard possession process — one more shield for you.
You can still claim even after you've moved out.

s4.title: Live-in landlord? (Lodger)
s4.intro: If you rent a room in the home the landlord lives in, you're a 'lodger' — deposit protection law does NOT apply. No scheme, no 1–3× penalty. Instead, demand:
items: A written agreement stating the deposit amount and the conditions for returning it.
A deposit receipt.
A move-in inventory of the room's condition, with dated photos.
The deposit must still be returned per the agreement — the inventory + photos are your evidence.

s5.title: Moving out
items: Deductions are only allowed with evidence (damage beyond fair wear and tear, unpaid rent).
Disagree with a deduction? Use the scheme's own free dispute resolution (DPS/mydeposits/TDS) — no court needed.
Photograph the room on moving-out day, just like the move-in inventory.
Review the landlord on RentAPlace — 'returned the deposit in full ✓' helps the next tenant and rewards good landlords.
